subject: geography
title: Drainage Basin: Stores Fill in Sequence, the River Lags
objectives: Describe the store sequence in order: interception fills first, the soil store fills next, percolation feeds the groundwater store last
Explain why discharge peaks after the peak rain (the lag) and why the recession is slow
State what switches on at soil saturation and what sustains the recession

definitions.meaning: The area of land drained by one river and its tributaries; in this animation one storm pulse crosses one basin and every store in it fills in sequence.
The leaves and surface litter that catch the first rain; it fills first and only begins to spill once it is full, which is why the hydrograph stays flat at the start of the storm.
The pore spaces in the soil that fill by infiltration once the interception store spills; when it saturates, overland flow switches on.
The water held in the rock below the soil, fed last by slow percolation; it empties last and sustains the river as baseflow during the recession.
Water running over the surface to the channel; it only switches on once the soil store saturates, and it makes discharge rise fast and peak after the rain eases.
The groundwater flow that sustains the river after the rain has gone; it is why the hydrograph recedes slowly instead of dropping at once.
The delay between the peak rain and the peak discharge, caused by the basin stores filling in sequence before fast flow reaches the channel.

mechanismSteps: Interception fills first: the storm arrives, the interception store catches the rain and only spills once full, while the channel and hydrograph stay flat (s1).
Soil fills next and groundwater starts last: the spill infiltrates and fills the soil store, and slow percolation only now starts feeding the groundwater store (s2).
Soil saturates and the river peaks late: at saturation overland flow switches on, discharge rises fast and peaks after the rain has already eased (s3).
The river recedes slowly on baseflow: the rain is gone and the surface stores drain, but groundwater baseflow sustains a slow recession (s4).
workedExample: Trace one storm pulse through the basin. Step 1 (s1): the interception store fills first and only spills once it is full, so the hydrograph stays flat while the rain is already falling. Step 2 (s2): the spill infiltrates, the soil store fills next, and slow percolation starts feeding the groundwater store last. Step 3 (s3): the soil store saturates, overland flow switches on, and discharge peaks after the rain eases - that delay is the lag time. Step 4 (s4): with the rain gone, the surface stores drain but the hydrograph recedes slowly, sustained by groundwater baseflow emptying last.

trap.misconception: The river peaks when the rain is heaviest, because rain runs straight off the surface into the river.
trap.explanation: The slip: Rain visibly falls on the whole basin at once and the river visibly rises, so it looks as if the rain reaches the channel immediately and the highest discharge must match the heaviest rain. The fix: The basin stores fill in sequence - interception first, then the soil store, then groundwater - and overland flow only switches on once the soil saturates, so discharge peaks after the peak rain and then recedes slowly, sustained by groundwater baseflow. In class, replay scene 1: freeze while the interception store is filling and ask where the rain is at that moment - held in the store, not in the river - which is why the peak cannot match the heaviest rain.
